EC1: Form of diagnosed psoriasis [NOT] other than chronic plaque psoriasis (i.e. guttate [OR], erythrodermic [OR], pustular)
EC2: Diagnosis of other active, ongoing skin diseases [OR] or skin infections that may interfere with examination of psoriasis lesions
EC3: Ongoing use of [AND] other psoriasis treatment including but not limited to topical [OR] or systemic corticosteroids [OR], other topical medications [OR] (i.e. coal tar), oral [OR] or biologic medications [OR] for the treatment of psoriasis, and UV therapy. The following washout periods will be required: 2 weeks for topical therapy; 2 weeks for phototherapy; 12 weeks for biologic or targeted therapies; 4 weeks for other systemic therapies
EC4: Use of oral estrogen therapy [AND], [NOT] excluding oral contraceptive pills
EC5: Women who are pregnant, nursing, or of child-bearing potential who are unwilling to use appropriate method(s) of contraception.
EC6: Patients unwilling to limit exposure to UV light
EC7: Current significant medical problems that, in the discretion of the investigator, would put the patient at significant risk
EC8: Patients with disorders of calcium metabolism [OR] and/or hypercalcemia
EC9: Use of any investigational drug within 4 weeks prior to randomization, or 5 pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamics half-lives, if known (whichever is longer)
EC10: History of allergy [AND] to any component of the IP
